USMC_1st_Tank_Battalion.historical_WATCHTOWER: Companies A and B landed on Guadalcanal in Aug 1942; A used M2A4, B used M3 light tanks. Company C was assigned elsewhere/Samoa rather than the initial landing.
USMC_1st_Tank_Battalion.branch_rule: WATCHTOWER is absent. The A/B tank companies therefore do not disappear from the theater; after Santo falls they are a plausible New Caledonia reinforcement.

IJA_1st_Independent_Tank_Company.historical: formed from veteran 4th Company, 2nd Tank Regiment; roughly company-scale 12 tanks; nine were destroyed in the Matanikau attack
IJA_1st_Independent_Tank_Company.branch_rule: No historical Matanikau attack. The company/hulls survive the historical loss gate and require reallocation.

IJA_8th_Tank_Regiment.historical: 8th Tank Regiment is listed under 17th Army / 8th Area Army at Rabaul by Nov 1942.
IJA_8th_Tank_Regiment.branch_rule: New Caledonia/Santo create at least as strong a South Pacific allocation motive as historical Guadalcanal. The regiment is therefore retained as a South Pacific commitment, not returned to the China/Five-Go wallet.

2nd_Tank_Regiment_4th_Co_or_1st_Independ.type: mainly Type97 Chi-Ha 57mm with a small Type95 component
2nd_Tank_Regiment_4th_Co_or_1st_Independ.arrival: follow-on heavy lift centered 1942-10-09..13, not necessarily first-wave

38th_Division_tankette_element.reason_for_uncertainty: historically detached South/Timor commitments make full-company transfer unsafe to assume

USMC_1st_Tank_Battalion_A_B.types: Company A M2A4; Company B M3 light tanks
USMC_1st_Tank_Battalion_A_B.reason: No Guadalcanal commitment; Santo loss and the visible threat to Noumea/Tontouta make defensive redirection high priority.

United_States.anti_tank_support: Marine 37mm AT guns remain an important part of the local armor fight; exact count will be drawn from the final 1st Marine Division residual OOB.

New_Caledonia_combat_first_pass.terrain: road-corridor fighting around Boulouparis-La Foa-Tontouta is more armor-usable than Guadalcanal jungle/sandbar, but bridges, mines, air/artillery and narrow routes keep tank packets small.
New_Caledonia_combat_first_pass.technical_exchange: US 37mm light tanks have a clear direct-fire anti-armor advantage over Japanese tankettes and can penetrate Chi-Ha/Ha-Go at common battle ranges. Japanese 57mm Chi-Ha is useful HE support but is not a comfortable frontal M3/M2A4 killer; Japanese artillery, mines, air and flank geometry must do much of the anti-tank work.

personnel_delta_vs_current_no_explicit_a.Japan_KWM: +100 to +400 net, because Marine tanks/37mm anti-tank fire outweigh part of Japanese armor's infantry-support benefit
personnel_delta_vs_current_no_explicit_a.Allied_KWM: +200 to +500 net from Japanese tracked support and additional artillery/air concentration around armored counterattacks

New_Caledonia_combat_first_pass.global_settlement: Existing Japanese 10-13k and Allied 8.5-11k ground casualty bands remain broad enough to contain this correction; centers should shift modestly upward rather than rewriting the campaign.

Rabaul_8th_Tank_Regiment.1942_11_26_presence: HARD working anchor from 8th Area Army OOB
Rabaul_8th_Tank_Regiment.pre_transfer_quality: full-strength-ish but old Type89-heavy regiment in late-1941/early-1942 descriptions

working_model_mix.Type97_or_Shinhoto: 0-4 by end-1942; later replacements can increase this

Rabaul_8th_Tank_Regiment.allocation: Rabaul/New Britain operational reserve and garrison. No centered transfer to New Caledonia before the Oct campaign; later company-sized reinforcement is sensitivity only.
Rabaul_8th_Tank_Regiment.national_accounting: PHYSICALLY SURVIVING BUT SOUTH-PACIFIC-TIED. Must be subtracted from any China/Manchuria 'free' armor wallet.

end_1942_south_pacific_tied_pool.other_local_armor: small Santo/Lunga/Port Moresby tankette/independent elements remain OPEN; no tank regiment is auto-created at Port Moresby
end_1942_south_pacific_tied_pool.meaning: At least roughly 45-60 useful tracked combat vehicles/equivalents are already tied to the Branch South Pacific at end-1942, before counting small garrison packets.

development_lesson: New Caledonia becomes a real pre-GALVANIC tank/AT experience: Japanese crews learn again that high-velocity 37mm fire is dangerous to thin armor and that reliable vehicles still require artillery/engineer/infantry integration. It reinforces 47mm/combined-arms development but does not yet justify a 75mm medium-tank emergency.
